pairs.why: B's locomotive is built more like a real engine, with piston rods linking the drive wheels and a believable cab and tender, while A is a simpler, rounder toy with decorative gold bands.
The two are nearly identical; A's chunky posts and smooth planks are a hair closer to the real pier, while B adds nail heads and a busy foreground shoreline.
A's glossy yellow straps and soft coral soles match the real flip-flops slightly better, though both put dots over the whole sole and B is a bit more matte.
A is a solidly built, glossy, chunky boot like the real cards' clean 3D objects, while B's stretched shaft and odd proportions don't read as a real boot, even though B's background matches better.
A matches the real glass's large tall shape, with the straw running diagonally through the juice and clear chunky ice, while B is smaller and more photographic.
A keeps the real card's small inset LEDs, soft matte-glossy orange body and stemmed earbuds, while B has oversized candy LEDs, bulbous earbuds and oversaturated color.
A has the smooth glossy yellow blades and rounded toy finish of the real fins, while B is flatter and more matte, with ribbed texture the lessons mark as too texture-y.
A's tilted thick target and fuzzy plush bear are closer to the real card, while B's bear and frame are smoother and more plastic-looking.
